text.en: In "the glory of the Lord", Handel puts "ry" and "of" on one note, the Italian way of joining two vowels. Other editions had moved the words; Ebenezer Prout's of 1902 put Handel's notes back: "It is just as easy to sing 'glo-ryof' ... in two syllables as 'glo-rious'."
text.es: En "the glory of the Lord", Handel pone "ry" y "of" en una sola nota, a la manera italiana de unir dos vocales. Otras ediciones habían movido la letra; la de Ebenezer Prout, de 1902, devolvió las notas de Handel: "It is just as easy to sing 'glo-ryof' ... in two syllables as 'glo-rious'" (es igual de fácil cantar "glo-ryof" en dos sílabas que "glo-rious").

source.en: Ebenezer Prout (editor), Handel, Messiah, full score (London: Novello, 1902), preface, p. vi; University of Toronto, Faculty of Music copy, read from the scan

text.en: Near the end Handel wrote "and the glory, and the glory of the Lord". Every printed edition leaves out the second "and", Prout's too, "the sense being quite complete without it", so the sopranos sing "and the glory, the glory, the glory of the Lord".
text.es: Cerca del final, Handel escribió "and the glory, and the glory of the Lord". Todas las ediciones impresas omiten el segundo "and", también la de Prout, porque "the sense being quite complete without it" (el sentido queda completo sin él), así que las sopranos cantan "and the glory, the glory, the glory of the Lord".
